papers.title_en: Key-Gram: Extensible World Knowledge for Embodied Manipulation
papers.authors: Jingjing Fan, Siyuan Li, Botao Ren, Zhidong Deng
papers.evidence: 使用关键语法检索的世界知识记忆用于具身操控
papers.tldr: 当前具身控制模型将语言知识与视觉计算耦合，导致模态竞争且知识扩展依赖骨干更新。Key-Gram提出条件记忆框架，通过哈希查找将指令分解为key-grams并检索语言先验，经门控融合注入骨干，实现语言-视觉分离。在RoboTwin2.0、LIBERO-Plus和真实任务上，Key-Gram分别提升骨干29.5%/9.9%、35.8%/4.5%和15.4%/8.1%。外部化语言记忆为改进组合基础、迁移和真实操作提供可扩展机制。
papers.abstract_en: Embodied control increasingly requires models to follow compositional language instructions while reasoning over dynamic visual states. However, current vision-language-action policies and world-action models often couple linguistic knowledge with visual computation in a shared backbone or conditioning pathway, leading to modality competition and making knowledge extension dependent on backbone updates. In this paper, we introduce Key-Gram, a conditional-memory framework that separates language-derived world knowledge from visual-state reasoning for embodied control. At its core is a memory module that decomposes an instruction into task-specific key-grams, retrieves static linguistic priors through deterministic hashed lookup, and injects the retrieved entries into selected hidden layers through context-aware gating and lightweight convolutional fusion. This design allows the backbone to devote its main capacity to visual reasoning and action inference, while reusable instruction knowledge is stored in an extensible external memory. The logical memory table can be conveniently partitioned during training and, due to its $O(1)$ lookup pattern, efficiently placed on host memory during inference. Across RoboTwin2.0, LIBERO/LIBERO-Plus, and real-world dual-arm manipulation, Key-Gram consistently improves both $π_{0}$ and $π_{0.5}$ backbones, with average relative gains of $29.5\%/9.9\%$ on RoboTwin2.0, $35.8\%/4.5\%$ on LIBERO-Plus transfer without target-domain fine-tuning, and $15.4\%/8.1\%$ on real-world long-horizon tasks. These results demonstrate that externalized linguistic memory provides an effective and extensible mechanism for improving compositional grounding, transfer, and real-world manipulation.

papers.title_en: PInVerify: An Offline Embodied Benchmark for Active Instance Verification
papers.authors: Yuhang Jiang
papers.evidence: 提出主动实例验证基准，需要导航至目标物体并进行语言描述匹配
papers.tldr: 现有具身代理在导航到目标物体方面取得进展，但在近距离多视角验证实例的细微属性差异（如颜色条纹）上存在不足。本文提出主动实例验证（AIV）任务，并构建离线基准PInVerify，包含3000个评估片段、18个类别、陷阱视图等。基线基于开源小规模MLLM（≤8B参数），采用属性分解、可见性加权多视角跟踪及三种NBV策略。最佳MLLM基线比最佳嵌入基线高4.9个百分点，LoRA微调达85.6%，但主动视角选择未带来可靠提升。PInVerify旨在推动具身AI中主动细粒度语义验证的研究。
papers.abstract_en: Embodied agents have made strong progress in navigating to target objects, but reaching the goal vicinity does not guarantee that the agent has found the correct instance: subtle attribute differences (e.g., "white floral" vs. "white striped") often require close-range, multi-view inspection. We address this gap with Active Instance Verification (AIV), a task in which an agent actively selects viewpoints around a candidate object to decide whether it matches a fine-grained natural-language description. We formalize AIV as a finite-horizon decision process and introduce PInVerify, an offline embodied benchmark for AIV: 3,000 evaluation episodes across 18 object categories, delivered as multi-view captures with a 6-sector navigation topology that exposes trap views (navigable but uninformative) and unreachable sectors. As reference baselines we build a training-free pipeline and a LoRA-fine-tuned end-to-end agent around open-source multimodal large language models (MLLMs) at on-device scale ($\leq$8B parameters), with attribute decomposition, a visibility-weighted multi-view tracker, and three next-best-view (NBV) strategies. In our evaluation across Qwen3-VL (4B/8B), SenseNova-SI-1.2-InternVL3-8B, CLIP, and SigLIP2, the best MLLM-based baseline exceeds the best embedding baseline by 4.9 pp; GT-box ablations show a +3.1 pp detection gap; and we do not observe reliable gains from active viewpoint selection within the tested NBV strategies. A LoRA-fine-tuned agent (SFT+GSPO) reaches 85.6%. PInVerify aims to support further work on active, fine-grained semantic verification in embodied AI. Code: https://github.com/Avalon-S/PInVerify.

papers.title_en: When Robots Do the Chores: A Benchmark and Agent for Long-Horizon Household Task Execution
papers.authors: Zilin Zhu, Longteng Guo, Yanghong Mei, Bowen Pang, Zongxun Zhang, Xingjian He, Ruyi Ji, Jing Liu
papers.evidence: 包含导航的长时程家庭任务基准与VLM代理
papers.tldr: 现有具身AI基准侧重短程导航/操作，忽略长程家务任务的高层规划能力。本文提出LongAct基准，通过抽象低级控制聚焦认知能力评估，并设计HoloMind智能体，采用DAG层次规划器、多模态空间记忆、情景记忆和全局评判器实现长程自主规划。在GPT-5和Qwen3-VL上的实验表明，HoloMind显著提升长程任务性能，但即使最强模型也仅达59%目标完成率和16%完全成功率，凸显长程规划的挑战。
papers.abstract_en: Long-horizon household tasks demand robust high-level planning and sustained reasoning capabilities, which are largely overlooked by existing embodied AI benchmarks that emphasize short-horizon navigation or manipulation and rely on fixed task categories. We introduce LongAct, a benchmark designed to evaluate planning-level autonomy in long-horizon household tasks specified through free-form instructions. By abstracting away embodiment-specific low-level control, LongAct isolates high-level cognitive capabilities such as instruction understanding, dependency management, memory maintenance, and adaptive planning. We further propose HoloMind, a VLM-driven agent with a DAG-based long-horizon hierarchical planner, a Multimodal Spatial Memory for persistent world modeling, an Episodic Memory for experience reuse, and a global Critic for reflective supervision. Experiments with GPT-5 and Qwen3-VL models show that HoloMind substantially improves long-horizon performance while reducing reliance on model scale. Even top models achieve only 59% goal completion and 16% full-task success, underscoring the difficulty of LongAct and the need for stronger long-horizon planning in embodied agents.

papers.title_en: Event-Grounded Sparse Autoencoders for Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.authors: Xinchen Jin, Aditya Chatterjee, Pranav Kumar, Rohan Paleja
papers.evidence: 使用稀疏自编码器对VLA策略进行可解释性分析
papers.tldr: VLA策略的隐藏表征直接影响闭环行为，但现有可解释性工具因输出为动作而非文本而难以迁移。本文提出事件锚定SAE流水线，通过聚类末端执行器关键帧将SAE特征与行为事件关联，并可选地利用VLM提供语义注释。在模拟和真实机器人实验中，事件锚定排名对OpenVLA和π0.5产生最强因果效应，但SAE作为干预基础存在架构依赖性和安全性局限。该方法为行为锚定的VLA可解释性提供了实用起点，推动了闭环行为层面的特征分析。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies translate language and visual inputs into robot actions, where their hidden representations directly shape closed-loop behavior. However, mechanistic interpretability tools from language and vision-language models do not transfer cleanly to VLAs: outputs are robot actions rather than human-readable tokens, and interventions can only be tested via expensive closed-loop rollouts. We propose an event-grounded interpretability pipeline that anchors SAE feature analysis to behavioral events rather than text contexts. End-effector keyframes are clustered within each task using visual, state, and temporal cues, linking SAE features to behaviorally salient events and, via optional VLM annotations, to semantic context. To our knowledge, our pipeline is among the first to ground SAE-based VLA analysis in closed-loop behavioral events. Across two simulation architectures and a real-robot study, event-grounded ranking yields the strongest causal effects on OpenVLA and transfers to the continuous action chunks of $π_{0.5}$. SAE is a sparse but imperfect intervention basis: usability varies with architecture and intervention site, and aggressive intervention reveals safety and interpretability limits. Overall, event-grounded SAE analysis emerges as a practical starting point for behavior-anchored VLA interpretability, motivating future work on SAE features beyond action-aligned coordinates, finer-grained closed-loop evaluation, and safe interventions for high-stakes VLA deployments. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/xc-j/Event-SAE}.

papers.title_en: PEDESTRIANQA: A Benchmark for Vision-Language Models on Pedestrian Intention and Trajectory Prediction
papers.authors: Naman Mishra, Shankar Gangisetty, C. V. Jawahar
papers.evidence: 行人意图和轨迹预测用于自动驾驶场景
papers.tldr: 行人意图与轨迹预测对自动驾驶安全至关重要。本文提出PedestrianQA，一个大规模视频问答数据集，利用自然语言标注将预测任务转化为带结构化理由的问答形式，使视觉语言模型(VLM)无需专门架构即可学习视觉动态、上下文和交互线索。在PIE、JAAD、TITAN和IDD-PeD基准上微调VLM后，意图分类、轨迹预测精度及解释性理由质量均显著提升，优于现有方法。该工作展示了VLM作为统一可解释框架在安全关键行人行为建模中的巨大潜力。
papers.abstract_en: Pedestrian intention and trajectory prediction are critical for the safe deployment of autonomous driving systems, directly influencing navigation decisions in complex traffic environments. Recent advances in large vision-language models offer a powerful new paradigm for these tasks by combining high-capacity visual understanding with flexible natural language reasoning. In this work, we introduce PedestrianQA, a large-scale video-based dataset that formulates pedestrian intention and trajectory prediction as question-answering tasks augmented with structured rationales. PedestrianQA expresses richly annotated pedestrian sequences, in natural language, enabling VLMs to learn from visual dynamics, contextual cues, and interactions among traffic agents while generating concise explanations of their predictions without needing specialized architectures tailored for each task. Empirical evaluations across PIE, JAAD, TITAN, and IDD-PeD show that finetuning state-of-the-art VLMs on PedestrianQA significantly improves intention classification, trajectory forecasting accuracy, and the quality of explanatory rationales, demonstrating the strong potential of VLMs as a unified and explainable framework for safety-critical pedestrian behavior modeling.
